note: Human rulings on out-of-scope differences in a candidate's receipt. Each rule names the field it covers and the candidate state it applies to, and says what the human accepts. ruling.ps1 turns each rule into a standing predicate on one step of the candidate, and records one ruling per episode and step through the member HTTP API (record_ruling). Nothing here is a verdict: the gate evaluates each ruling on every probe its selector reaches, and a probe that fails it becomes violates_ruling.

rules.label: x-request-id is an opaque random id, not identity
rules.reason: The order does not mention a request id. A random UUID per response identifies the request and carries no user name, so it is accepted. A value that carries a user name is not accepted by this rule and would be reported as violating it.

rules.label: the over-limit answer is 429
rules.reason: The status differs only where the candidate answers 429 to a request over the limit. The order asks for 429 there, so the status step is accepted at that step.

rules.label: a 429 answer has no link body
rules.reason: The base answers the same request 201 with a link, and the over-limit answer has no link body. Accepted where the candidate answers 429.

rules.label: the over-limit body carries an error or a generated value
rules.reason: A rejected request creates no link, so later generated values (codes, paths, counts) can differ from the base. The field is accepted when the candidate has a value; the value itself is not compared.

rules.label: the session cookie is a random token per login
rules.reason: The session cookie is issued per login and holds a random token, so its value differs between runs. The field is accepted when the candidate sets it; the value is not compared.

rules.label: the stored user id is a generated identifier
rules.reason: The stored user's id is generated on signup, so its value differs between runs. The field is accepted when the candidate stores the user; the value is not compared.

rules.label: the stored password hash is salted per write
rules.reason: The stored password hash is salted when it is written, so its value differs between runs with the same password. The field is accepted when the candidate stores a hash; the value is not compared. This is a human relaxation of the comparison, recorded as such: the predicate checks presence, not that the value is a hash.
